The money was always gone before the month was, and being the one who could make it stretch made her feel useful, so she kept taking more on — school forms for her cousins, interpretation at neighbors' appointments, the family's tax paperwork by fifteen. Nobody meant anything by it; her parents were proud of her, and she liked being needed. She moved out at nineteen already fluent in two languages and one habit: handle it quietly so nobody else has to worry.
